title: Deliver the internal linking map from the ten heaviest pages, with exact anchors and destinations
description: For the ten pages that carry the site: home, /pricing, /about, /products/channels, /products/buzz, /products/files, /solutions/bootcamps, /solutions/schools, /solutions/universities and /resources. For each page, list the outgoing internal links that should exist: the exact anchor text, the destination URL, and the one journey or query the link serves. Also record the links that exist now, so the change can be counted, and flag any page that receives no internal links at all, because an orphan page cannot rank however good it is. Deliver as a prioritised table: the first ten links to add (highest value first), then the rest, with the file or component in zedu-fe that renders each source page so the change is addressable. No code change: the map is the deliverable. 60 points because this covers ten pages both ways (what exists and what should), not a single page audit.

goal.title: Build an internal linking map for zedu.chat by Fri 20 Nov
goal.description: Map how every public zedu.chat page links to the others, find orphan pages and weak links, and propose links with anchor text. Done when: a table of pages, current links, recommended new links and anchor text is delivered and reviewed by Fri 20 Nov.

workstream.title: Map internal links from the ten heaviest pages, where the links would matter most
workstream.description: An internal linking map over every page is work nobody will finish. The deliverable does it for the ten heaviest pages first, because those are the ones with the most traffic and the most to gain, and it lists for each one the pages it should link to and the anchor text to use, so a writer can act on it without deciding anything. The map is produced from the live sitemap and the live navigation rather than from a list of pages we remember, and it comes with the pages we are deliberately not linking to and why, so the map does not turn into link spam.
